title: Separating perception from reasoning in vision-language models: a model-free render ceiling for crystal structures
authors: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban
abstract: Multimodal evaluations cannot say whether a vision-language model misread an image or misreasoned about it, because every existing method for separating the two places a second model in the loop. We introduce the render ceiling, a model-free reference for benchmarks built by rendering known objects: inverting the frozen cameras and re-solving cross-view correspondence recovers exactly the answer the images support. We prove the ceiling fails only through an enumerable set of projection coincidences and certify that set empty on 2,160 rendered crystal structures, so every point of a model's deficit belongs to the model. Across fourteen vision-language models, supplying exact geometry as text lifts every model yet closes under half the gap for thirteen, while a supervised vision model with no language component reads the same images at 0.8952, above every vision-language model. The instrument exposes extraction-stage fabrication that downstream accuracy would misattribute to reasoning, yields camera-placement rules for benchmark builders, and transfers to any benchmark with an invertible forward rendering.
summary: This paper introduces the 'render ceiling,' a novel, model-free benchmark designed to rigorously separate perception failures from reasoning failures in vision-language models. By using rendered crystal structures, the authors demonstrate that a purely vision-based model can outperform complex VLMs, exposing that much of the apparent reasoning ability in current models is merely sophisticated pattern matching based on image extraction.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a model-free method to separate whether a vision-language model fails due to poor image perception or flawed reasoning about the image content.
main_result: The authors introduce the 'render ceiling,' a model-free benchmark that certifies model deficits, showing that a purely vision-based model outperforms most vision-language models on crystal structure tasks.
method: They construct the render ceiling by inverting frozen camera views and re-solving cross-view geometric correspondences, bypassing the need for a secondary, potentially flawed, model.
model_or_system: The study uses crystal structures as the physical system, testing vision-language models (VLMs) and supervised vision models on tasks like crystal system prediction from multiple rendered views.
key_observables: Accuracy scores against the model-free render ceiling ($R_1$), and the decomposition of error into 'perception share' and 'residual' components.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed on 2,160 rendered crystal structures, and the performance is compared across fourteen different VLMs.
main_assumptions: The render ceiling is only guaranteed to fail through an enumerable set of projection coincidences, which was confirmed to be empty for the tested structures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the model-free attribution instrument across different data 'rungs' (e.g., true positions vs. rendered geometry vs. text geometry); Figure 2 shows how the ceiling drops when camera views are withheld.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of separating perception from reasoning, introduces the model-free render ceiling using crystal structures, presents quantitative comparisons across various models, and analyzes the resulting error decomposition.
why_interesting: While the subject is AI/ML, the rigorous, model-free benchmarking methodology and the use of deterministic geometric reconstruction to test model boundaries are highly relevant to developing robust simulation tools in physics.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

Figure 4 No vision–language model reaches the certified ceiling, and the supervised pixel baseline outscores all of them. Zero-shot crystal-system accuracy: seventeen vision–language model arms across ten vendors, together with the supervised pixel baseline, which is not a vision–language model. Four arms clear the shape-free baseline (solid line, 0.5286) and the best reaches 0.7333 against the oracle ceiling of 1.0000; dashed line: seven-way chance, 0.1429. Error bars are 95% confidence intervals. Run-to-run spread of majority voting is a mean of 5.0 of 210 structures across two sweep runs.
